subject: Biology
description: Mouth to anus pathway, enzymes (amylase, pepsin, trypsin, lipase), absorption sites

questions.stem: The CHEMICAL DIGESTION of starch begins in the:

options.option_text: Stomach, by the action of pepsin enzyme
Mouth, by salivary amylase (ptyalin)
Small intestine, by the bile and lipase
Large intestine, by gut bacteria action

questions.explanation: Starch digestion begins in the MOUTH via SALIVARY AMYLASE (also called PTYALIN). Breaks long starch chains into shorter dextrins + maltose. Pause in stomach (acid stops salivary amylase) → resumes in small intestine via PANCREATIC AMYLASE. Final hydrolysis to GLUCOSE by maltase, sucrase, lactase at intestinal villi brush border. Distractor 1 — stomach is for protein (pepsin). Distractor 3 — bile + lipase digest fats, not starch. Distractor 4 — large intestine handles undigested fibre.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: PEPSIN, the enzyme that digests proteins in the stomach, works best at pH:

options.option_text: Around 7, the neutral pH range
Around 1.5-2.0, the strongly acidic range
Around 8-9, the alkaline pH range
Around 5.5, the slightly acidic range

questions.explanation: Pepsin — secreted as inactive PEPSINOGEN by chief cells of stomach; activated by HCl (from parietal cells) to active PEPSIN. Optimum pH 1.5-2.0 (strongly acidic). Breaks proteins → peptides. PROTON PUMP INHIBITORS (PPIs — omeprazole, pantoprazole) block HCl secretion, raise pH, reduce pepsin activity → used for ulcers, GERD. Most other enzymes work at NEUTRAL or slightly alkaline pH (e.g., pancreatic enzymes in duodenum work at pH ~7-8).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Most NUTRIENT ABSORPTION in humans takes place in the:

options.option_text: Stomach, the J-shaped digestive sac
Small intestine, with millions of villi
Large intestine (mostly water absorption)
Oesophagus, the food pipe to stomach

questions.explanation: Small intestine — ~6 m long. Inner surface enormously increased by FOLDS, VILLI (~1 mm projections), MICROVILLI (brush border on each villus) → total absorptive surface ~250 m² (size of a tennis court!). Each villus has capillaries (carry sugars, amino acids) and a LACTEAL (lymphatic vessel; carries fats). Large intestine — absorbs WATER + electrolytes; gut bacteria synthesise vitamin K + some B vitamins; stores faeces. Distractor 1 — stomach absorbs little (some alcohol, drugs). Distractor 3 — water + minerals only. Distractor 4 — purely a passage.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: BILE secreted by the liver helps in the digestion of:

options.option_text: Proteins, breaking them into amino acids
Fats, by emulsifying them into small droplets
Starches, breaking them into sugar units
Nucleic acids, breaking them into nucleotides

questions.explanation: Bile is NOT an enzyme — it's a fat-emulsifier. Bile salts (cholic acid, deoxycholic acid) coat large fat droplets, breaking them into tiny droplets → much larger surface area for PANCREATIC LIPASE to act on → fatty acids + monoglycerides. Without bile, fat digestion would be very slow. Bile also neutralises acid coming from stomach. Stored + concentrated in GALLBLADDER. Distractor 1 = pepsin (stomach), trypsin (small intestine). Distractor 3 = amylase. Distractor 4 = nucleases.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: TRYPSIN is a digestive enzyme that:

options.option_text: Digests fat in the small intestine area
Digests proteins in the small intestine
Digests starch in the mouth and saliva
Activates other enzymes in the stomach acid

questions.explanation: Trypsin — pancreatic enzyme; breaks proteins / polypeptides into smaller peptides in the small intestine. Secreted as inactive TRYPSINOGEN, activated by ENTEROKINASE (from intestinal cells). Trypsin then activates other pancreatic proteases (chymotrypsinogen → chymotrypsin). Optimum pH ~8. Distractor 1 = LIPASE. Distractor 3 = amylase. Distractor 4 = enterokinase / pepsin. Note — pancreas also secretes amylase (carbs) + lipase (fats); 'pancreatic juice' contains all three.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The PERISTALTIC MOTION of the gut moves food forward by:

options.option_text: Gravity pulling food downward only
Wave-like contractions of smooth muscles
Air pressure pushing food through the gut
Cilia movements lining the gut wall

questions.explanation: Peristalsis — coordinated contraction + relaxation of CIRCULAR + LONGITUDINAL smooth muscle layers. Pushes food forward in a wave. Begins in oesophagus, continues throughout GI tract. Independent of gravity — that's why astronauts can eat in zero-G. Controlled by ENTERIC NERVOUS SYSTEM ('second brain'). Constipation often relates to weak peristalsis. Vomiting = REVERSE peristalsis. Distractor 1 — gravity helps in oesophagus but isn't the mechanism. Distractor 3, 4 wrong.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The APPENDIX in humans is considered:

options.option_text: A vital organ for digesting fat efficiently
A largely vestigial organ with some immune role
A storage place for excess water absorbed
A part where bile production takes place

questions.explanation: Appendix — small finger-like pouch attached to caecum (start of large intestine). VESTIGIAL in humans — once useful for digesting cellulose-rich plant matter (still functional in herbivores like rabbits). In humans, recent research suggests immune-system role + 'safe house' for beneficial gut bacteria after diarrhoea. APPENDICITIS — inflammation; medical emergency requiring surgical removal (appendectomy). Removal has no major impact on health. Distractor 1 — fat is digested by bile + lipase. Distractor 3 = colon. Distractor 4 = liver.
